text_blocks.snippet: The highest death rates are generally found in infancy and old age, specifically those aged 85 and older. While death rates are relatively high at birth, they decline sharply in early childhood. Then, rates begin to rise again in adolescence and increase exponentially from adulthood onwards. The oldest age groups (85+) consistently have the highest crude death rates, according to USAFacts.

list.title: Adolescence and Young Adulthood:
list.snippet: Death rates increase again, particularly in adolescence due to factors like motor vehicle accidents and other unintentional injuries.

list.title: Middle Age:
list.snippet: Death rates continue to rise, with unintentional injuries, heart disease, and cancer being leading causes.

list.title: Old Age (85+):
list.snippet: Death rates are highest in this group, driven by diseases associated with aging, such as heart disease and other chronic conditions.
